A real-life night-shift simulation

Presentation and ARIA concept by Kelly Dianga · 2 August 2026

Start the night shift

Begin with the road-safety problem and the intervention gap, then follow one driver through proactive engagement, a medium-band fatigue event, a high alarm and ARIA’s follow-up. The rail on the left carries the shift state throughout.

01 · The problem and the gap

Fatigue is common. In an HGV, the consequences are disproportionate.

Driver fatigue is estimated to contribute to 15–20% of serious road crashes. Professional truck drivers are a recognised high-risk group because long, irregular and night-time work concentrates the conditions that produce fatigue.

Existing systems are essential: they assess alertness and warn the driver. ARIA is needed because the mandated function stops at detection and warning; not sustained, human-centred support before the alarm or a structured next step after it.

Why the intervention layer mattersEU road safety evidence
15–20% of serious road crashes are estimated to involve driver fatigue European Commission fatigue report
4–5% of police-reported European crashes involve HGVs but their consequences are more severe
13.8% of EU road deaths involved an HGV in 2023 2,829 fatalities
Existing systems Assess alertness, detect reduced attention and issue a warning through the vehicle HMI. Fleet DMS products may also record or forward the event.
The gap The regulatory requirement does not provide a companion layer for the period while the driver is fading below the high alarm, or structured support once the alarm has cleared.
ARIA’s role Use time and vehicle context proactively, respond to an exposed medium-risk state with haptic and brief voice interaction, then support the driver’s next safe decision after an alarm.
Sources: European Commission — Fatigue thematic report · European Commission — Professional drivers of HGVs and buses, 2025 · EU DDAW requirements
02 · What ARIA is

A companion layer for the driver.

ARIA works to keep the driver alert and responds when existing detection says the driver is starting to fade.

Detection stays with the systems that already do it well.

ARIA’s role

ARIA operates in the space before the alarm and after it.

Never instead of it. It has no control path to any other device.

04 · Safety gate

ARIA does not speak just because the road looks boring.

Monotony creates a reason to engage. The motion-only safety gate decides whether ARIA may speak in the next few seconds.

Motion-only clearanceGate open

May speak

  • Stable speed
  • No braking
  • No indicators
  • Low steering variance
  • Sustained quiet window

Stay silent

  • Braking
  • Indicating
  • Steering demand
  • Co-driver present
  • High alarm active
05 · Proactive engagement

Before any alert, ARIA opens one short exchange.

Long continuous driving, late-night timing, a quiet cab and an open gate make a brief check-in appropriate.

ARIA initiates only when it expects an answer. After acknowledgement it goes quiet and starts a conversational cooldown.

Proactive exchangeVoice only
Quick one, what city is known as the Steel City?
Sheffield.
That’s it. I’ll leave you to the road.
Short spoken response provides the engagement
06 · Reactive engagement

The existing DMS exposes a medium-band state.

The signal sits below the high-alarm threshold. ARIA can tolerate this noisier band because the cost of a false positive is a brief friendly question, not a siren.

The DMS keeps ownership of detection and of its high alarm. ARIA consumes only the real-time sub-threshold state.

DMS fatigue severityMedium
Sub-thresholdMedium → ARIAHigh → DMS

Debounce and hysteresis prevent ARIA from firing repeatedly when the score hovers around the boundary.

07 · Driver-facing intervention

First, a seat pulse. Then a short decision.

Haptic feedback cuts through the noise of a truck cab without becoming another blaring sound.

ARIA can suggest a stop. If the driver cannot stop immediately, it can bridge with bounded retrieval-based trivia until the planned break.

Medium-band responseHaptic + voice
You’re starting to fade. Can you take the next safe break?
Not yet — I’m booked in, but my break is due soon.
08 · Stop or bridge

ARIA supports the next safe decision, it does not take over.

The driver cannot stop immediately, so ARIA begins a bounded trivia bridge. Then the DMS severity rises to high.

The moment the high threshold is reached, ARIA stops mid-sentence and yields to the existing alarm.

Can stop

ARIA names the next safe break, then goes quiet.

Cannot stop yet

Short retrieval questions, bounded by the gate, a hard cap and driver opt-out.

One quick one while we bridge, which planet is known as the Red—
Sub-thresholdMediumHIGH
09 · High alarm

ARIA does not compete.

The existing DMS fires its own warning, unaltered. ARIA is silent in the moment and records only that its intervention did not prevent escalation.

No ARIA speech is layered onto the alarm. The driver receives one clear safety event.

!

EXISTING DMS ALARM

High-severity fatigue event detected.
ARIA voice channel: silent

10 · After the alarm

ARIA waits, then goes straight to the decision.

Follow-up happens only after the alarm clears, a settling period passes and the safety gate opens again.

ARIA does not ask whether he is tired. It already knows. It offers stop or bridge, once per window.

Follow-up conditionsAll met
High alarm clearsThe existing DMS remains fully independent.
Settling periodARIA waits so it does not feel like the second half of the siren.
Safety gate reopensStable motion and no active high alarm.
That alert was serious. Take the next safe stop, or say “bridge” if you cannot stop yet.
11 · Serious cases and transparency

Most interaction stays in the cab.

A fleet notification is reserved for serious cases: no speech after a high alarm, or repeated high events within a defined window.

The policy may be configurable, but it is never secret. The driver is told what is collected and who can see it.

What leaves the cabMinimal event state
Normal caseDriver respondsCAB ONLY
Serious caseNo speech after highNOTIFY
Serious caseRepeated high eventsNOTIFY
BoundaryNo vehicle controlREAD ONLY
BoundaryNo warning suppressionUNTOUCHED
12 · How the information reaches ARIA

ARIA combines signals

The production system would use approved, read-only integrations. The first prototype simulates them to prove ARIA’s behaviour.

Vehicle + tachographMoving, continuous driving, speed, braking, indicators, steering variance, driver session
→
ARIA context modelTime, interaction history, cooldown, monotony trigger and motion-only safety gate
→
Voice + hapticProactive exchange, medium-band response and post-alarm follow-up
Prototype: simulated journey timer, mocked DMS events, predefined road-demand states and experimenter-controlled conditions. It proves the intervention logic without pretending to have truck integration.
ARIA · Closing

ARIA is not another system watching the driver.

It is the human-centred layer that helps the driver stay awake, respond calmly, and keeps existing safety systems useful because they no longer get switched off.
